scope: Approximate present surviving Chihaya Castle earthwork ensemble: four principal enclosure grounds, southeastern enclosure, southwestern terrace, two current Chaya-no-dan outwork steps and narrow main-bailey northwest/west/south banks. Original current terrain shape and slope breaks retained. All nine bounded ground perimeters except the native lower-context ring are explicit authoring estimates; no archaeological survey, exact medieval edge/date or original grade is asserted. This is current ground form, not a restored medieval castle. Modern shrine/office/pavilion/Zondokan buildings, steles/signs/trees and undetectable lost ditch reconstructions are separate context; the whole natural hill is review terrain, not a castle solid.
method: One explicit current-ground scope disposition for each of nine independently authored constituents. These are membership records, not mesh rays, archaeological survey controls or a census of every minor forest terrace. Principal ordering and surrounding northwest/south enclosures follow primary village factual text; current Chaya-no-dan association follows the society first-person site-visit account. Original numerical source terrain and mapped routes/later-building positions locate the bounded estimates.

limitations: Unmeasured outer edges, construction phases and original medieval grades remain approximate. Source-data resolution is not archaeological accuracy.
Current primary village account says the main surface is not clearly flat and former ridge-cut defences are not clearly identifiable. No absent flat floor or ditch is manufactured.
Modern buildings only locate current precincts; they are not castle geometry. No later-building roof outline is used as an estimated ground perimeter.
Native historical fourth-bailey-sized polygon is only the lower context. Whole-castle coverage includes the separately located upper and outwork constituents.

Bank strip is a current uneven ground approximation, not a surveyed flat belt or masonry wall. Small plan-edge overlaps and gaps inherit estimated perimeter limits; source-ground surface itself is retained.
Source grade is current digital terrain, not medieval reconstruction. Absolute registration to live host/Terrarium remains unverified and current-world activation is off.

sources.use: Primary factual text on present uneven main ground, surrounding northwest/south enclosures and currently indistinct former ditch cuts; no page pixels.
